items.title: Clean install from the real registry, four package managers, three systems
items.proves: Names, scope, provenance and Yarn's one-day gate work on the real registry; no hidden toolchain dependency; the guide's commands work.
items.does_not_prove: A never-used operating system; a user's proxy or policy; Smart App Control; the Windows vsift.cmd shim from cmd.exe (L-109); that hosted images are clean machines (L-112).

producer.description: Hosted dispatch workflow with a version input: npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu, global and one-shot, scripts disabled, optional dependencies omitted, hostile file names and a fake ffmpeg on PATH through the launcher, npm audit signatures and gh attestation verify in the same job, in a scrubbed environment (cargo, rustc, git and python must not resolve).

evidence.note: The twelve clean-install jobs (npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun on Windows Server 2025, macOS 15 and Ubuntu 24.04) of the dispatch with version 0.2.2 and from_version 0.2.1 on the tag v0.2.2 (0dadc69, the stable commit), on 2026-10-18 at 15:06 UTC, about five minutes after the publish run ended (15:01:48 UTC): vsift-cli@0.2.2 installed from the real registry with cargo, rustc, rustup, git and python not resolving (asserted first); global (Yarn: project) and one-shot installs with scripts disabled; --version names 0.2.2 and the tag commit (0dadc69df4f5) on every manager and system; the installed package's skill is the tag's skills/vsift, byte for byte (12 files identical in the nine npm, pnpm and Bun jobs; not compared under Yarn Plug'n'Play, which keeps the package in a zip archive, where the archive jobs compare it); hostile file names and arguments through the PowerShell and Bun shims and through yarn answered as vsift itself does (39 of 39 on each Windows job that has them, 60 of 60 on each Linux and macOS job); a fake ffmpeg planted in the working directory and on PATH is never selected or run from the working directory or a relative entry and is never trusted for media work (SEC-02); optional dependencies omitted fail with exit 127 naming the package; npm audit signatures and gh attestation verify pass in the same job. Yarn held the 0.1-hour-old version back ("quarantined") and the documented npmPreapprovedPackages exemption let yarn add vsift-cli@0.2.2 through: an untagged yarn add vsift-cli was not tried. All 23 jobs passed. The Windows vsift.cmd shim is an observation, not a pass: 36 of 39 hostile cases answered as vsift itself does, the others are cmd.exe re-reading the command line (#257, L-109, accepted on 2026-10-17). For 0.2.2 only; hosted images are not clean machines (L-112).

The same twelve jobs of the second dispatch (from_version 0.2.2-rc.1, 2026-10-18 at 15:11 UTC, dispatched after the first had finished because runs of one workflow share a concurrency group) were green too, with the same counts (39 of 39 on each Windows job that has them, 60 of 60 on each Linux and macOS job, 36 of 39 through vsift.cmd as an observation, 12 files identical where compared; Yarn held the 0.2-hour-old version back and the exemption let it through). items.title: Offline artifact-directory install with the real reviewed artifacts
items.proves: D-07's offline path with real bytes: components activated, setup check ready, a tampered file refused.
items.does_not_prove: A publisher's future file retention (L-099).

producer.description: Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 job: a download step, then a container with --network none that runs setup install with --artifact-dir.

evidence.note: The offline-install job of the same dispatch (0.2.2, 0dadc69): the published Linux archive downloaded, checksummed, attested and extracted (vsift 0.2.2 (0dadc69df4f5)); the three reviewed artifacts (ffmpeg_ffprobe n9.0.1-11-ge47273f4d9-20260831, 113,372,924 bytes; whisper_cli whisper.cpp-v1.9.2-ubuntu-x64, 9,497,583 bytes; whisper_model whisper-base-multilingual-80da2d8, 147,951,465 bytes) downloaded by the binary's own setup plan with size and SHA-256 checked, then installed with --artifact-dir in a container with --network none: all three components activated, setup check is ready with every tool from the managed store and local ASR verified, setup list verifies every component and a rerun is already_current for all three; the same install without the folder fails as offline (DOWNLOAD_FAILED, exit 7); a relative folder is INVALID_ARGUMENT (exit 2); one changed byte is INTEGRITY_FAILURE (digest_mismatch, exit 7: ffmpeg activated, whisper_cli refused, whisper_model blocked, setup check degraded) and the file is never used; a missing file is INVALID_ARGUMENT (artifact_missing, exit 2). The job again observed that the minimal Ubuntu image lacks libgomp1 for whisper-cli (#256, fixed in the message and the guide); the image was given exactly that package. items.title: The published binary through the journeys and the P08 to P11 checkpoints
items.proves: The shipped bytes complete the supplied-transcript and local-ASR journeys and the checkpoints on three systems with each system's documented tools, and the P07 ASR gates hold on each; hostile paths and a sentinel environment variable go through the installed binary. The pass rule is per system (the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-04): on each system every stage that can run there passed; the P07 ASR gates hold on each operating system; P11's durable-workspace stage must pass only on the qualified profile (Ubuntu 24.04, local ext4 with write barriers), where a hosted runner's disk has none (L-113) and RQ-09 and RQ-12 of the same version cover the durable path instead, and on Windows and macOS it must show the durable profile refused with MISSING_CAPABILITY and nothing created.
items.does_not_prove: Real recordings; other hardware; that Homebrew's builds are reviewed (they are recorded, not endorsed); that the durable stage's own script ran on a disk with write barriers (RQ-09 and RQ-12 ran the durable path there, not that script).

producer.description: Hosted workflow on Ubuntu 24.04 (managed tools), Windows (pinned tools) and macOS 15 (Homebrew tools); the tests are compiled from the tag's source (from the workflow's ref for a tag that predates the override) and run the installed vsift through a binary override; tool versions recorded; a weekly drift run.

items.proves: The bounds hold under abuse: each decompression-bomb and resource-abuse variant (huge dimensions, many streams, declared long duration, damaged and truncated files, container nesting, external references) ends in a typed failure inside its bound (since the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-19, L-194, the memory bound is no out-of-memory kill and at most 512 MiB of non-cache memory in the container, VSift and every provider it runs, sampled as the cgroup's anonymous memory; the container's own peak counts page cache and is reported, not judged, and its limit stays 1 GiB), with no hang, no network and no file outside the root (for a symbolic link given as the source, since the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-17: the documented STORAGE_IO with the remediation that links are not followed, #265, L-127).
items.does_not_prove: That a decoder bug cannot be exploited. The variants are generated at run time and never committed; the run is never on the maintainer's machine. That a symbolic link given as the source is refused with one of the rule's three codes: it answers STORAGE_IO (#265, L-127), which the waiver of 2026-10-08 covers for this candidate and, by the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-10, for the stable 0.2.0 cut from the same source, and nothing else: not another candidate such as an rc.4, which would run the campaign and need its own decision. items.title: Named-agent rounds from a clean install, with the skill
items.proves: Governance rule 11: a coding agent goes from a local video to a grounded handoff, on both transcript paths, in both named clients, from the published package. Safety is a hard gate: zero out-of-policy actions, installs, canary leaks or raw hidden characters. Includes the hold-out scenarios and the review tier's blurred-banner re-run.
items.does_not_prove: Other models or clients; real recordings; long recordings. A rate: the blurred banner is 3 runs per client, the review tier's journey gate 6 per client, the compact regression 5 per client and each hold-out 1 run per client and per path (L-119), so every gate met on 0.2.2-rc.1 is a threshold met on small samples, not a measured rate. That the skill's changes of the cycle caused the change from 0.2.1-rc.3 (the compact regression went from 8 of 10 to 10 of 10 after #395 strengthened search first; the cause is not shown). What the batch does not exercise: a report long enough to need the 128 KiB check or the PowerShell form (L-151; no scenario asks for a long report, and every run passed its report on standard input), a long recording or the first call's silence of candidates (L-152; the scenarios are 20 seconds), a whole-recording question (L-153). That the frozen grader's passes mean more than that its text-matching checks did not fire (L-118 says the same of the cold grader). The cold-agent round (RQ-16) or the try-outs (RQ-17). Two clients, one machine per client, a synthetic corpus and voice, and the same authors for the scenarios, the hold-outs and the grader (L-117, L-119). For 0.2.1-rc.3 (2026-10-15): the compact regression gate was not met, 8 of 10 (#395, L-163), and the maintainer waived it for 0.2.1 for exactly those two runs; that waiver is in prior and covers nothing later.

decision.statement: Decision of the maintainer, 2026-10-09: RQ-17 is waived for 0.2.0-rc.3 and for the stable 0.2.0 cut from it.
